title: En resumidas cuentas: en síntesis, en pocas palabras

sections.content: En resumidas cuentas (in short, to sum up) signals that what follows condenses everything said before into its essential point. It's a natural way to close a paragraph or an argument, much like "in short" or "all in all" in English. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: En resumidas cuentas, casos como el de Bolivia en 1952 y el de Costa Rica en 1948 demostraron que no existía una única fórmula para lograr un cambio duradero.
items.english: In short, cases like Bolivia's in 1952 and Costa Rica's in 1948 showed that there was no single formula for achieving lasting change.

items.spanish: En resumidas cuentas, la reforma constitucional demostró ser una herramienta de doble filo a lo largo del siglo.
items.english: In short, constitutional reform proved to be a double-edged tool throughout the century.

items.spanish: En resumidas cuentas, ni el crecimiento económico sostenido de algunos países ni programas pioneros como Progresa lograron, por sí solos, cerrar la brecha de desigualdad.
items.english: In short, neither some countries' sustained economic growth nor pioneering programs like Progresa managed, on their own, to close the inequality gap.

items.spanish: En resumidas cuentas, la región entró al nuevo milenio habiendo aprendido, a un costo enorme, muchas de las lecciones de su propio siglo XX.
items.english: In short, the region entered the new millennium having learned, at an enormous cost, many of the lessons of its own twentieth century.

sections.content: En resumidas cuentas sits at the start of a sentence, usually followed by a comma, and works best when summing up several ideas at once -- reserve it for a genuine conclusion, not just any transition.
